video_title: Zach Pandl: Why Grayscale Says It's Time to Buy Bitcoin
gist: Grayscale research head Zach Pandl argues crypto bottomed in June 2026 after an October 2025-June 2026 drawdown, and that the rebound held up through a Fed hike and the CLARITY Act failing because Strategy stabilized its leveraged balance sheet. He frames Bitcoin and gold as the 'third way' against structural US debt debasement and values L1 tokens as commodities where size and fees matter. His standout calls: Zcash is underpriced at about 1.5% of Bitcoin's market cap, energized AI compute (including Bitcoin miners) is a buy after a ~30% drawdown, and digital asset treasury companies are underrated. (The record sits in a Michael Howell/CrossBorder Capital folder, but the transcript is a 51 Insights interview with Zach Pandl.)

themes.theme: Cycle bottom and the buy call

insights.claim: Grayscale's research head says crypto found a durable bottom in June 2026, after a large drawdown from October 2025, and that now is a good entry point for long-term allocations.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: A large institutional crypto manager is explicitly telling clients to deploy capital now.
insights.quote: our confidence since the end of June has been rising week by week essentially that we found a bottom in the asset class

insights.claim: Pandl reads the crypto rebound continuing despite a Fed rate hike and the CLARITY market-structure bill failing to pass as evidence that the market was oversold and that the bottom is durable.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: When price shrugs off bad news, it often confirms that selling pressure is exhausted.
insights.quote: Fed rate hike, clarity not passing and yet we've seen a big rebound. I think that's a sign the market was oversold

insights.claim: The 2025-26 drawdown closely followed the four-year halving cycle on the way down, but the bottom came in June rather than the November that cycle-followers expected, so investors tied to the cycle missed the upswing.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Timing entries off the halving calendar is becoming unreliable; investors should not wait for a cycle-dated bottom.
insights.quote: if you were too wedded to the cycle, you missed some of this upswing

insights.claim: Pandl expects the four-year halving cycle to fade, but says crypto will keep having prolonged cycles because Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana are commodities, and commodities like oil, gold and copper show momentum and autocorrelation in price.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Trend-following and buying drawdowns, rather than halving dates, are the right tools for timing crypto exposure.
insights.quote: I think the industry will always have cycles uh because they are commodities

insights.claim: Pandl says the most important driver of Bitcoin's rally in recent months was Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) stabilizing its balance sheet, after pressure on its levered structure and especially its Stretch product, by selling some bitcoin and managing investor expectations.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Strategy's financing health is a key short-term swing factor for BTC, and a seller that has stabilized removes an overhang.
insights.quote: the most important thing in the last few months has been micro strategy or now known as strategy has been getting its balance sheet stabilized

insights.claim: Pandl ranks Bitcoin's drivers as follows: structural debasement risk first, then the interest-rate cycle (higher real rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding Bitcoin and gold), then risk appetite and equity performance, then shorter-term ETF flows and futures liquidations.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Gives a ranked checklist for explaining and forecasting BTC moves the way FX strategists treat currencies.

insights.claim: Pandl predicts Bitcoin will trade above its previous all-time high before the end of 2027.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Implies meaningful upside from current levels within about a year.

insights.claim: Pandl calls unchecked US government debt growth the single most important durable macro trend, and says that without massive tax increases or spending cuts, which have no political will behind them, debt will keep rising and weigh on the dollar.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: This is the core structural bid for hard assets and against long-duration dollar claims.
insights.quote: We have a deep problem that we don't raise enough taxes essentially to pay for social services spending and everything else and there's no political will to deal with those uh things.

insights.claim: Comparing global currencies, Pandl finds that every major fiat alternative, including the euro and the Chinese yuan, has similar debt problems, which leaves non-government currencies (gold and Bitcoin) as the 'third way'.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Rotating between fiat currencies does not hedge debasement; non-sovereign assets do.
insights.quote: There is no kind of good option. And therefore you need to think about the the third way. And the third way is basically non-government currencies.

insights.claim: Pandl argues 'debasement trade' is a misleading label because the trend began about 18 years ago with the September 2008 Lehman bankruptcy, quantitative easing, TARP and the rise of populist politics, and is structural rather than a short-term trade.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Supports sizing hard-asset positions as long-term holdings rather than tactical trades.

insights.claim: To hedge dollar debasement, Pandl recommends shortening duration and avoiding long-duration fixed fiat cash flows (bonds), and favoring short-duration income, floating cash flows such as cash-flowing companies and alternative yield like the crypto basis trade, plus real assets like commodities and real estate (with valuation caveats).
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: A concrete portfolio playbook: underweight long bonds and overweight short duration and real assets.
insights.quote: the things that are most at risk are long duration fixed cash flows in fiat currency, otherwise known as bonds

insights.claim: Pandl, a former head of currency strategy at Goldman Sachs, says global investors should hold Chinese yuan-denominated assets, since the yuan is 'a little peanut' in international markets today and will likely play a bigger global role, and he also suggests emerging-market currencies more broadly.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: A non-consensus call to diversify into CNY assets as a hedge against the dollar's global role.
insights.quote: despite China's mega size, the Chinese yuan is a little peanut in international markets today

insights.claim: Asked to pick one asset to hold for 10 years without selling, Pandl chose Bitcoin over gold, calling it an easy choice.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Signals a strong long-run preference for digital over physical hard money.
insights.quote: Bitcoin. Easy choice.

insights.claim: Pandl says Bitcoin already sits on national balance sheets through sovereign wealth funds in Central Asia, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, but not on central bank balance sheets. Central banks favor gold because of history (Bretton Woods) and maturity, and the People's Bank of China and the central bank of Russia have been big gold accumulators since Russia invaded Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Central bank buying is a large untapped demand source for BTC, but it will come last.
insights.quote: central banks will be the very last buyer of of these things and they need to see all these boxes being checked

insights.claim: Pandl expects central bank adoption of Bitcoin to take roughly the next five years, after the industry deals with AI-driven cybersecurity threats, post-quantum readiness and privacy.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Sets a multi-year timeline for the sovereign demand catalyst; progress on quantum and privacy are the milestones to watch.

insights.claim: Pandl says quantum progress is far enough along that post-quantum cryptography readiness should be well underway in blockchains and is happening, though there is no need to panic, and it remains uncertain whether quantum computers will ever break classical cryptography (Peter Shor's 1994 algorithm).
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Treats quantum risk as a manageable software-upgrade issue rather than an existential sell signal.
insights.quote: this is software. Software can be changed. It will change if and when it needs uh to change.

insights.claim: Because of chain-specific risks such as quantum and the range of use cases beyond digital scarcity, Grayscale advises sovereign wealth funds to hold a mildly diversified crypto basket rather than Bitcoin alone, while still calling Bitcoin the king of its category by a huge margin.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Institutional allocation guidance favors BTC-led baskets over a BTC-only position.

insights.claim: Pandl names Zcash as the asset the market is most mispricing. Even after an enormous run over the past year, it trades at about 1.5% of Bitcoin's market cap, which he calls surprisingly low.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: An explicit relative-value long call on ZEC versus BTC from Grayscale's research head.
insights.quote: its relative market cap at one and a half% still seems surprisingly low

insights.claim: Pandl frames Zcash as Bitcoin's 'Solana moment': just as Solana showed that different design choices can bring value against Ethereum in smart contracts, Zcash shows that privacy, AI-hardness and quantum readiness can win value against Bitcoin in the currencies category.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Implies the store-of-value category may support a meaningful number-two asset, as smart contracts did.
insights.quote: what can be thought of as Bitcoin's Salana moment

insights.claim: Pandl highlights privacy as a key gap between Bitcoin and gold: gold's transaction history can be obscured but Bitcoin's cannot, and this opens the way for privacy-focused stores of value like Zcash.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Privacy is a structural demand driver for privacy coins and a feature Bitcoin may need.
insights.quote: You cannot obscure the transaction history of Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Grayscale values layer-1 tokens as commodities using statistical supply-demand models rather than cash flows, and finds that size matters: larger networks (activity, users, assets, trading, fees, TVL, RWA) earn nonlinearly higher token values.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Implies a scale premium: favor the largest networks and the challengers able to reach escape velocity.
insights.quote: the TLDDR is that size matters. Bigger is better. Bigger networks mean bigger token value.

insights.claim: If he could use only one metric to value an L1 token, Pandl would pick transaction fees paid, because fees are the least gameable statistic compared with incentive-driven activity metrics.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Fees are the metric to screen L1s on and to discount incentive-inflated activity numbers against.
insights.quote: Fees paid are somebody's money going in out of their pocket into somebody else's pocket. So, it's very difficult to game it

insights.claim: Pandl rejects 'fat protocol is dead' arguments in favor of a 'fatter protocol' thesis: unlike TCP/IP, which captures zero value on the information internet, value-layer protocols like Ethereum and Solana clearly capture more than zero, though how value splits among L1s, L2s and apps is still open.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Defends L1 token value capture against the narrative that apps and L2s take all the economics.

insights.claim: The host cited data points against fat-protocol value capture: Robinhood's new Ethereum-tech chain earned about $800,000 in its first two weeks while only around $500 went to Ethereum as fees, and Solana settled roughly $3.5-3.8 billion in tokenized stocks in June while the SOL price stalled.
insights.speaker: host (Mark)
insights.so_what: Suggests L2s and tokenization volume do not automatically flow through to L1 token holders.

insights.claim: Pandl says the most important form of value capture from blockchains is 'value leakage' to users through a cheaper, lower-risk financial system, with remaining value spread across L1 tokens, application tokens, public equities and intermediaries, so a diversified digital-asset portfolio should own all of them.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Argues for spreading exposure across tokens and crypto equities rather than concentrating in L1s.

insights.claim: Pandl puts approximate market caps at about $300 billion for Ethereum, about $100 billion for BNB Chain and about $70 billion for Solana, calls these three today's clear L1 leaders, and says much of their growth is already priced in.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Asymmetric upside likely sits in smaller challengers rather than the incumbents.

insights.claim: Among smaller L1s, Grayscale's current bets on emerging leaders are Sui and Avalanche, and Pandl says some of the best trades will be $5-10 billion networks that grow to hundreds of billions in market cap.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Names specific mid-cap L1 longs with a 10x-plus upside framing.
insights.quote: The ones that we've made our bets on at the moment are SUI and Avalanche

insights.claim: Grayscale's working assumption is a multi-chain world with strong network effects: about half a dozen high-value smart contract platforms (including perhaps one or two L2s, which carry an L2 discount), about 100 lower-value niche chains, and many private consortium, compliance and subnet chains. By its count, about 40 smart contract chains are currently analyzable.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Value will concentrate among a few winners, so L1 picking matters more than broad L1 baskets.

insights.claim: Pandl sees tokenized capital markets as a 20-year journey in which bigger networks keep getting bigger and accumulate value.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Supports a long-horizon thesis for the leading tokenization platforms.
insights.quote: tokenized capital markets are going to be a 20-year journey

insights.claim: Pandl frames the AI stack as compute (energy into computation), models (computation into intelligence) and apps/agents (intelligence into value). He argues the top layers face open-source competition and falling pricing power, while all demand funnels down to compute, which stays scarce.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Favor the compute layer over richly valued model and app companies that are possible IPO candidates.
insights.quote: all roads lead to more compute

insights.claim: Pandl notes that GPU rental costs are still rising while AI token prices fall, evidence that compute remains the scarce resource in the AI stack.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Pricing power sits with compute owners, not model providers.
insights.quote: token prices are going down GPU rental costs are going up so you still have scarcity there

insights.claim: Permitted electricity access is a key bottleneck for compute, and many current or former Bitcoin miners hold it, so 'energized compute' stocks offer a blend of AI compute beta and Bitcoin beta.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Bitcoin miners with grid power are levered to both AI demand and BTC price.
insights.quote: one of the elements of scarcity is permitted electricity access and there are still a lot of players that are former or current Bitcoin miners that are sitting on that uh access

insights.claim: After a roughly 30% drawdown in neocloud and compute stocks (the host cited 27% since late September, with neoclouds spending more than twice their revenue on capex), Pandl calls them good entry points. He prefers a diversified basket of neoclouds, powered-shell data centers and grid-connected miners to balance leverage, and plugs the Grayscale Compute ETF (GCPU).
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: A buy-the-dip call on AI infrastructure, with diversification to manage single-name leverage risk (and a promotional interest in GCPU).
insights.quote: I think after a 30% draw down uh these are good entry points uh in these names

insights.claim: Pandl sees the crypto-AI sector, which Grayscale tracks in a crypto sectors framework built with index provider FTSE Russell, as the category with the most long-term upside relative to its tiny current value, and expects one or more hundred-billion-dollar projects to emerge from it. Its current leaders are Bittensor, Near, World (Worldcoin) and Venice, followed by about 20-30 smaller tokens.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: For high-risk allocations, crypto-AI tokens are the sector Grayscale flags for asymmetric upside.

insights.claim: Pandl calls Bittensor misunderstood and extremely interesting, describing it as 'Silicon Valley on the blockchain', a system that ties together talent, capital, competition and customers to create innovation clusters, mostly but not necessarily AI-related.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: TAO is a named favored pick in crypto-AI over the more widely touted Near.
insights.quote: bit tensor to me is a misunderstood and extremely interesting uh thing. I like to call it the call it Silicon Valley on the blockchain

insights.claim: Pandl calls digital asset treasury companies underrated at current prices, saying some are great assets trading at a discount, under the principle that there are no bad assets, only bad prices.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: DATs trading below their underlying holdings may be a value opportunity.
insights.quote: there are no bad assets. There are just bad prices.

insights.claim: Pandl says traditional finance is again in a 'blockchain not Bitcoin' phase and that Bitcoin, despite being the largest and most established crypto asset, will be the last thing TradFi understands.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: Institutional underappreciation of BTC relative to tokenization narratives leaves room for future flows.
insights.quote: the last thing Treadfi will understand is Bitcoin which is hilarious because it's like by far the biggest and most established uh thing

insights.claim: Pandl says spot ETFs lowered crypto's risk profile by bundling custody, liquidity, tax handling, staking and account types into one instrument, bringing in investors unwilling to self-custody. He notes crypto's 50-100% volatility now looks too tame for some frontier investors and still too risky for ultra-conservative ones.
insights.speaker: Zach Pandl
insights.so_what: As risk falls, more conservative capital pools come into range, which supports structural inflows.
